title: Paradroid
build: Hewson's original UK disk of 1985, a GCR image of the protected original from the C64 Preservation Project; booted through the collection's patched copy, whose game data is byte for byte the same (orientation.md)

credits.role: Design and programming: "Paradroid programmed by Andrew Braybrook", as the game's own pages credit it
"Sound advice", as the game's own pages credit it

tools.host: Linux x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04, no display (cloud container)

accuracy.note: the deck drawn from the listing against a recorded frame of play

exclude: not used: nothing in the game reads or writes them
not used: past the colour scheme's 16 entries
not used: the KERNAL's work area, which the game, with the ROMs switched out, leaves alone
not used: what the boot file and the KERNAL left there, below the robot slots
padding after the sound driver: the RAM's stripes of $00 and $FF, which nothing reads
padding after the memory editor, the same stripes, which nothing reads
padding after the code, the same stripes, which nothing reads

runtime: cleared by the restart ($10FF), then the blank character set of the band above the deck (irq_top), shape 0, the blank sprite irq_bottom shows over the status line, and the dictionary index at $4400-$45FF (index_words); as loaded, the staged copy of $D000-$D7FF that the start-up copies there
runtime: the screen and its sprite pointers; as loaded, the staged copy of $D800-$DBFF that the start-up copies there
runtime: the work shapes $44-$4F, the mirrored halves of a console picture (mirror_shape) and the eight numbered droid shapes (sprite_number); as loaded, the staged copy of $DC00-$DEFF
padding after the version mark, the same stripes, which nothing reads
padding after the interrupts, the same stripes, which nothing reads
runtime: the deck map, 64 rows of 256 cells, built for each deck (build_deck) and holding the title pages on the title; as loaded, the staged copies of $E000-$FFFF, $C000-$CFFF and $0500-$07FF
padding after the waypoint lists, the same stripes, which nothing reads
padding after the title pages, and below it what the load left there before the start-up's copies, which nothing reads
padding after the high score strings, the same stripes, which nothing reads
runtime: two spare bytes, then the NMI, reset and interrupt vectors, which cold_start and the interrupts write
include: the title pages, in the RAM under the I/O

regions: the robot slots, the open doors, the saved sprites and the population table
the colour table, a group for each character
sprite shapes: the 001's shots and the explosions
sprite shapes: the console pictures, the shots and the menu pictures
status words, console strings, lifts, collision rules and colours
the dictionary of the droid descriptions
the transfer board's rows and the high score strings
the per-deck tables, the side view and the 16 deck plans
